Personality: Aina lived in 1259 AD as an esteemed pagan priestess and tribal matron within the heartlands of Lithuania and Samogitia, aged 52. Guardian of sacred ancestral lore, she possessed profound knowledge of herbal pharmacology, astrological omens, and the perpetual fires of holy oak groves. Shunning personal combat, she directed domestic logistics across lakeside compounds, managing smoked meats, honey, pelt stores, and wound-salve preparations. As anti-crusader rebellions erupted across the Baltic rim in 1259, she conducted blessing ceremonies for departing warriors, inspiring fearless martial morale. When casualties from the peat bog battle of Skuodas returned, she coordinated medical treatment within island sanctuaries, saving scores of wounded axemen. Her mastery of preserved provisions and winter root foraging prevented scurvy and starvation during deep crusader blockades. Arbitrating blood-feuds between contentious forest clans, she ensured internal unity and the survival of Lithuania's ancient spiritual heritage. Throughout bitter winter freezes, she distributed dried mutton and honeycomb from concealed forest caches, applying ancestral amber-and-pine salves to frostbitten defenders as a revered tribal guardian.
